# `lakana access`

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py from the Typer app. Do not edit by hand:
run `uv run python scripts/generate_reference.py` and commit the result. -->

Part of the [Command line reference](../cli.md), which lists the options for every command.

Usage: `lakana access [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Explain who may do what, and keep access in a file.

## `lakana access explain`

Usage: `lakana access explain [OPTIONS] {principal}`

Show what PRINCIPAL may do on an object, and through which grant, role or group.

One row per action that applies to the object: `allowed` is the answer of the same check the server makes when the principal tries, and `via` names the grants that give it (a role, a single action, or either through a group). You may explain yourself; explaining someone else needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRINCIPAL` | text | required |  |
| `--scope` | text | none | The object: ENV, ENV/NAMESPACE or ENV/NAMESPACE/TABLE. Leave it out for the instance. |

## `lakana access export`

Usage: `lakana access export [OPTIONS]`

Write the live access as an access file.

The file lists the groups, service accounts, grants, row filters, column masks and CI trust rules of the scopes, in the format `lakana access plan` reads; planning it unedited plans nothing. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance.

The file format: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/reference/access-file/.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--scope` | text, repeatable | none | `instance` (the default) or an environment; repeat it for several environments. |
| `--output-file`, `-o` | path | none | Write the file here instead of printing it. |

## `lakana access plan`

Usage: `lakana access plan [OPTIONS] {file}`

Show what applying an access file would change, and every problem that stops it.

Nothing is changed. Prints `+` for what would be created, `~` for a CI trust rule changed in place and `-` for what would be removed, then access in the file's scopes that did not come from it (drift). Exits 1, with every problem on stderr, when the file has any. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance.

The file format: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/reference/access-file/.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | path | required | The access file, such as access.yaml. |
| `--allow-lockout` | flag | off | Accept a file that drops your own ADMIN role while another administrator remains. |

## `lakana access apply`

Usage: `lakana access apply [OPTIONS] {file}`

Make an access file's changes in one audited transaction, or none of them.

Without `--plan-fingerprint` the command plans the file, shows the plan and asks before it applies exactly that plan. With `--plan-fingerprint` it does not ask: that plan was the review. With `--output json` it shows no plan and so does not ask: pass `--yes` or `--plan-fingerprint`. In CI, pass `--yes` and the fingerprint of the plan step: the apply is refused, with nothing changed, when the file or the access changed since that plan. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance and a personal access token.

The file format: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/reference/access-file/.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | path | required | The access file, such as access.yaml. |
| `--plan-fingerprint` | text | none | The fingerprint `lakana access plan` printed: applies without asking, since that plan was the review. Without it the command plans first, shows the plan and asks (the command asks only when it plans itself). |
| `--source-commit` | text | none | The commit the file came from (7 to 64 hex digits), recorded with the apply. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Do not ask before applying; for CI. |
| `--allow-lockout` | flag | off | Accept a file that drops your own ADMIN role while another administrator remains. |

## `lakana access status`

Usage: `lakana access status [OPTIONS]`

Show the scopes access files manage and the changes made outside them.

Lists each managed scope with the file, commit, administrator and time of its last apply, then the overrides no apply has taken into account yet. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance.
